refutations.evidence: Per-fold model avg/trade vs always avg/trade (5 traded folds): 2024H1 0.698 vs 0.553; 2024H2 0.183 vs 0.226; 2025H1 0.221 vs 0.269; 2025H2 -0.075 vs -0.112; 2026H1 0.685 vs 0.638. Pearson corr(model_avg, always_avg) = 0.978, Spearman = 0.90. Sign agreement = 100% (5/5) — when always is +, model is +; on the only losing fold (2025H2) both are negative. Selection fraction averages ~88% in the four 2024-2026 folds (595/660, 517/557, 354/400, 409/464); only 2024H1 (210/447, 47%) is selective. Decomposition of the claimed +0.299% vs +0.174% all-folds baseline: FOLD-TIMING (always on same 5 traded folds = +0.3154% minus all-9-fold baseline +0.1739%) = +0.1415%; WITHIN-FOLD SELECTION (model +0.2988% minus always-same +0.3154%) = -0.0166% — NEGATIVE. Model beat always within-fold in only 3/5 folds and underperformed in aggregate. Across 8 random seeds the selection component is consistently negative: mean -0.017%, std 0.0007%, range [-0.0182, -0.0166], 0/8 seeds with positive selection. The whole-sample always-trade mean = +0.157% (matches prior +0.16% finding, below +0.30% threshold). The 4 abstained folds (2022H1/H2, 2023H1/H2) were skipped because the champion was still NeverTrade during walk-forward warmup (first learned champion only at fold 2024H1), not by predictive judgment; 2022H1 (-0.703%) and 2022H2 (-0.083%) were the worst folds, and excluding them mechanically inflates the mean.
refutations.reasoning: The model is a near-perfect levered/selective shadow of always-trade, not a source of stock-selection alpha. Per-fold returns correlate 0.978 with always-trade and sign-track it 100% of the time — pure event/market beta. The decomposition is decisive: the entire +0.125% the model adds over the all-folds always baseline comes from FOLD-TIMING (+0.142%, i.e. only trading the later 2024-2026 era), while genuine within-fold stock selection is NEGATIVE (-0.017%). Worse, that 'fold timing' is not skill — the early 2022-2023 folds were abstained on solely because the champion was still the NeverTrade warmup default before any model had trained, an artifact of walk-forward ordering rather than a prediction that those folds were bad. In the folds it actually trades, the model trades ~59% of events overall but ~88% in four of five folds and earns slightly LESS per trade than blindly trading everything. This is stable across 8 seeds (0/8 with positive selection). The 'edge' is regime/era selection plus warmup luck, the underlying sample is +0.157% (below the +0.30% tradability bar), and realistic costs are already baked in. No real, durable, tradable selective alpha — refuted.

refutations.evidence:
Buyback net returns are regime-split, not signal-driven. Raw per-fold always-trade mean net return: 2022H1 -0.703%, 2022H2 -0.083%, 2023H1 +0.614%, 2023H2 +0.175%, 2024H1 +0.553%, 2024H2 +0.226%, 2025H1 +0.269%, 2025H2 -0.112%, 2026H1 +0.638%. Pooled: pre-2024 (folds model ABSTAINED) = -0.019%/trade over 2,273 trades; 2024+ (folds model TRADED) = +0.315%/trade over 2,528 trades. The model abstained in exactly the flat/negative regime and traded in exactly the positive regime — it rode a regime shift, it did not select a signal.

The headline comparison is rigged by mismatched baselines. Model +0.299%/trade (2,085 trades, 5 folds) is compared to always-trade +0.174% computed over ALL 9 folds (4,411 trades, including the bad 2022-2023 folds the model skipped). Apples-to-apples — always-trade restricted to the SAME 5 folds the model traded — gives +0.315%/trade (2,528 trades), which BEATS the model by 0.017pp. The model UNDERPERFORMS naive always-trade on the identical periods.

The model is barely selective: in its traded folds it takes 2,085/2,528 = 82.5% of available trades (90%+ in 2024H2-2026H1). Per-fold it loses to always-trade in 2 of 5 folds (2024H2, 2025H1).

Threshold-selection lags the regime: it missed 2023H1's +0.614% and 2023H2's +0.175% (abstained), then stayed in for 2025H2's -0.112% (lost -0.075%/trade). Seed test (random_state 0/7/13/42/99): folds traded are identical, model avg 0.297-0.299% — stable, but stable around a non-edge.

Both model (+0.299%) and the matched always-trade (+0.315%) sit at/below the project's +0.30% tradability threshold, consistent with the prior loop-1-12 finding that realistic T+1 buyback edge was +0.16% (untradable).
refutations.reasoning: The "positive policy with breadth" verdict is an artifact of two flaws. (1) Regime dependence: buyback returns flipped from ~0/negative (pre-2024) to positive (2024+); the model's abstain-then-trade pattern simply tracks that flip rather than identifying a persistent cross-sectional signal. This is the same failure mode flagged for supply_contract. (2) A baseline-mismatch sleight of hand: the +0.299% vs +0.174% comparison pits the model only over its favorable folds against an always-trade number diluted by the unfavorable folds the model skipped. On a fair same-periods basis, naive always-trade (+0.315%) beats the model (+0.299%). The model adds no selective value — it takes 82.5% of trades and loses to always-trade in 2 of 5 traded folds and on the pooled same-period comparison. Seed-stability is real but irrelevant: it stably reproduces a regime bet, not an edge. Net of the realistic 0.313% cost the matched return barely reaches the +0.30% tradability bar and is essentially the same as buy-everything-recently. This is regime beta plus a misleading baseline, not a durable, tradable selective edge.

refutations.evidence: Reproduced exactly: model 2085 trades +0.2988%/trade vs always-trade 4411 +0.1739%. SELECTION LIFT IS NEGATIVE: in the 5 folds the model trades, buying ALL 2528 events yields +0.3154% vs the model's selected +0.2988% = -0.0166% lift; selected-vs-rejected Welch t=-0.30 (no winner-picking skill). The +0.299%>+0.174% gap is pure fold-selection (model abstains in 2022H1 -0.703%, 2022H2 -0.083%, etc.). SLIPPAGE: model already has 2x5bps=10bps slip; +20bps extra -> +0.099% (below +0.30% threshold), +40bps extra -> -0.101% (negative). If 'realistic 20/40bps' is per-side: model -0.001% at 20bps/side, -0.401% at 40bps/side. SIGNIFICANCE: per-trade t=2.25 (sd 6.05%, se 0.133%, 95% CI [+0.039%, +0.559%]); but per-fold paired diff vs baseline = +0.027%, t=0.78 (NOT significant, only 5 folds, 1 negative). Bootstrap P(mean<=0.174% baseline)=0.172, P(mean<=0.30% threshold)=0.503. CAPACITY: max_open_positions=1 deploys only 150/2085 (7%) of signals, mean drops to +0.078%; 847 signals/yr vs ~50 sequential slots/yr -> >90% undeployable. Seed-stable (+0.297% to +0.299% across seeds 0/1/2/7/42/123) but that does not rescue it.
refutations.reasoning: The +0.299% is not a tradable selective edge. (1) The 'learned policy' adds no selection skill: it underperforms trade-everything within the same folds (-0.017% lift, t=-0.30). The headline beat over the +0.174% baseline is entirely a regime artifact -- the policy abstains in the four early/bad folds and trades the good ones, exactly the 'fitting a regime' failure the script's own docstring warns against. (2) The edge does not survive realistic frictions: buybacks are often small/mid-cap and illiquid, so 5bps/side slippage is optimistic; at a plausible 20-40bps the net mean falls below the project's own +0.30% tradability threshold or goes negative. (3) It is statistically indistinguishable from the baseline (per-fold diff t=0.78; bootstrap gives a 50% chance the true mean is below the +0.30% bar). (4) Capacity constraints (max_open_positions=1) make >90% of signals undeployable and crush the realized per-trade return to +0.078%. This is consistent with the prior project finding that realistic T+1 execution cut buyback edge to +0.16%, below tradability. The 'POSITIVE POLICY WITH BREADTH' label is an artifact of measuring per-trade average over a regime-selected subset rather than genuine out-of-sample selective skill.

synthesis.honest_summary: All three reviews refute the claim, and every load-bearing number reproduces exactly from the on-disk artifacts. Two independent things must be kept separate. (1) "The learning machine works" — TRUE as a software/methodology claim: the champion/challenger walk-forward trainer is leak-free (challenger trains only on folds before the validation fold, champion is scored genuinely out-of-sample), it has a synthetic planted-edge sanity path that proves it CAN learn when edge exists, and it is seed-stable. (2) "Buyback is tradable" — FALSE as an edge claim. The headline "+0.299% beats +0.174%" is a baseline-mismatch artifact: the +0.174% baseline is always-trade diluted across all 9 folds including the bad 2022-2023 folds the model never traded, while the model is measured only over its 5 favorable folds. On a fair same-period basis, naive always-trade returns +0.3154% and actually BEATS the model's +0.2988% — the within-fold stock-selection component is NEGATIVE (−0.017%), and the model wins in only 3 of 5 traded folds (per-fold paired t=0.78, not significant). The model's per-fold returns correlate 0.978 with always-trade with 100% sign agreement and it trades 82.5% of available events (88%+ in four of five folds), so it is a near-pure shadow of buy-everything, not a stock-selector. The entire apparent lift comes from FOLD-TIMING (+0.142%): the model abstained in the pre-2024 regime (pooled −0.016%/trade) and traded the 2024+ regime (+0.315%/trade) — but that abstention was NOT a prediction, it was a mechanical warmup artifact (the champion was still the NeverTrade default with champion_version=0 until the first promotion at fold 2024H1, confirmed in both the fold CSV and trainer code). The underlying whole-sample buyback return is +0.157%/trade, matching the prior loop-1-12 finding of +0.16% and sitting well below the project's +0.30% tradability threshold; even the matched always-trade (+0.315%) barely touches that bar and degrades below it under plausible extra slippage (buybacks skew small/mid-cap) and the max_open_positions=1 capacity constraint that leaves >90% of signals undeployable. So: the machine is honest and works; buyback simply has no durable, tradable selective edge — what looks like edge is regime beta plus a misleading baseline plus walk-forward warmup luck.
synthesis.pdf_sentence: The offline learner's "positive policy with breadth" on buyback events is not a tradable edge: its apparent +0.299%/trade beat over the +0.174% always-trade baseline is an artifact of comparing the model only over its favorable 2024-2026 folds against an always-trade number diluted by the early folds it skipped, and on a matched same-period basis naive always-trade (+0.3154%) actually beats the model (+0.2988%), with the within-fold stock-selection component being negative (−0.017%) and statistically insignificant. The model abstained in the flat/negative pre-2024 regime and traded the positive 2024+ regime only because the walk-forward champion was still the NeverTrade warmup default before any model had trained — a mechanical ordering artifact, not a prediction — so its "edge" is regime beta plus a misleading baseline. The underlying whole-sample buyback return is +0.157%/trade, consistent with the earlier +0.16% finding and below the +0.30% tradability threshold; the learning machine itself is sound and leak-free, but the buyback data contains no durable selective edge to exploit.
